_comment: The witness register (#57). One entry per export-bearing census entry — the 156 whose mechanism in
parity/census/classification.json is one of the five dual-run sections. A witness is the rule joining a
captured trace back to the export it proves was driven, and it is what makes coverage here derived from
runs that actually happened rather than declared by whoever last edited a table.
export    the census entry this witnesses. An export the census no longer carries fails as stale
selector  dom only: compounds separated by whitespace — `*`, or a tag with any number of `.class`,
`[attr]`, `[attr=value]`, `[attr~=value]`, `[attr*=value]`. Whitespace is the descendant
combinator and it is the only one
names     the other four sections: the runtime names that would prove the export. Many-to-one in
places — NodeMouseHandler is the type behind onNodeClick, onNodeMouseEnter and several more
note      optional, and required by nothing: written where the rule needs defending, because a witness
that matches something the scenario did not really drive is how a derived number goes wrong,
and it is only findable if the rule is visible
Which kind an entry takes is not its own to declare — it follows the section the census puts the export
in, so a witness describing a trace shape that does not exist is a hard error rather than a finding.
A witness does not say the corpus reaches the export. That is what the traces say. An export whose
witness nothing holds is a hole, and holes.json is where the reason lives — the two registers are
different claims and neither stands in for the other.
For the change unions a name is a discriminant rather than a handler: `onNodesChange:position` reads
"some onNodesChange call carried a change of type position". Witnessing NodeAddChange by the handler
alone would count it driven the moment a mount fired one dimension change.
The hooks, api and props names were written before #59 built the probes: the hook's own name, an
imperative method's name, and — for props — the probe id naming which props type reported. A probe that
names one differently makes its export read as an undeclared hole, which is
the loud failure and the intended one.

witnesses.note: the class an edge wrapper carries for type `default`, which is the type BezierEdge is registered under
the container div is drawn by GraphView whether or not anything is portaled into it, so the descendant is the question
NodeResizer is the only thing that renders a `line` variant; a bare NodeResizeControl defaults to `handle`

ReactFlow mounts a provider itself unless one already wraps it, so every mounted flow runs this component. The selector cannot tell an explicit provider from the internal one and never could: the dom section is rooted at `.react-flow`, and what an explicit provider buys — hooks outside the flow — renders outside that root
same shape as EdgeLabelRenderer — GraphView draws the empty container for every flow, so only its content witnesses the export
align lands in the toolbar's transform, which getNodeToolbarTransform computes; the selector proves a toolbar was positioned, not that a non-default align was
the description a node points at is rendered from the aria-label config
the resolved class, which is what tells ColorModeClass apart from the ColorMode a consumer sets — `system` resolves to one of these two

nothing in the DOM is unique to the default options — they are merged into edges that declare none — so the witness names the shape a fixture exercising them should take: a `defaultEdgeOptions.type` of smoothstep over edges that declare no type. It shares its selector with SmoothStepEdge on purpose, and both are holes until such a fixture exists
the reference on the edge path, where EdgeMarker is the definition it points at

the class an edge takes from a type no built-in registers, the way NodeTypes shows up as react-flow__node-<key>. No fixture passes an edgeTypes map, so this names the key such a fixture is expected to use
the selection a held selectionKeyCode produces — the one key code with DOM of its own. The delete key codes are observable only as what is no longer there, which no selector can ask for

every node's transform is computed through the origin, so the export is reached by any mount. That no fixture sets a non-default origin is a *behavior* left undriven rather than an export, and it belongs to the hand-declared count — which has no rows until #58 implements the bucket, so today it is written down here and nowhere else
a node type no built-in registers, so the class names the fixture's own key. A fixture that renames it makes this read undriven, which is the loud failure rather than the quiet one

the attribution is what proOptions.hideAttribution removes. Its presence proves the option was read and left at its default — the *hiding* is what no fixture asks for, and that is a behavior rather than an export
the rect exists only while the pointer is down, so a scenario that completes its drag never records one — `selection-box-mid-gesture` is the reserved scenario that will
the z of a node's x/y/z, which is the part of the triple with DOM of its own

upstream wraps each edge in an svg whose z-index the mode computes, so any flow with edges reaches the export. Which of the two modes was in force is a *behavior* rather than an export, and belongs to the hand-declared count — which has no rows until #58, so today it is written down here and nowhere else
the second argument onConnectEnd is handed, which is the only place this type surfaces
the second argument onConnectStart is handed
the single argument the handler is called with
the event argument every resize handler is handed
the handler type behind the same three props OnSelectionDrag names; upstream declares both
the options record a hook is called with rather than a prop the flow is passed, so what records it is a probe installing the hook
as UseOnSelectionChangeOptions
the instance is proved by any method only it carries — the viewport helpers ride on it too but are their own export
the store's own shape, reached through useStoreApi().getState() rather than through the instance
the options record every viewport helper takes last
any one of the helpers proves the bundle
a probe id rather than a hook name: the props section is keyed by probe, and the probe names which props type reported
